claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications", series "Defense Futures", published 2010-11-01 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2010-07-20, DIA document number DIA-08-1011-005. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.

claims.text: Author of record per the DIA letter of 9 January 2018, item 35: "Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices, Dr J Golightly, Lockheed Martin."
The released cover page reads "01 November 2010 / ICOD: 20 July 2010 / DIA-08-1011-005." The author line is redacted under (b)(6).

A late-tranche DIRD. Its Intelligence Cut-Off Date of 20 July 2010 and DIA-08-1011 series number place it with the November 2010 batch rather than the FY2009 March-April 2010 tranche that carries ICOD 1 December 2009.

connections.note: Lockheed Martin appears three times on the DIA list: this paper, Dr V Teofilo's "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion," and Dr S Macheret's MHD air-breathing propulsion paper. Eric Davis said in a June 2018 interview that the advanced nuclear fusion for aerospace propulsion work was done by colleagues at Lockheed Martin, which matches the list. This is a direct, documented thread from the DIRD series into the prime-contractor cluster.
